info.name: Sally-K API — Checkout (Cart, Orders, Payments, Rewards)
info.description: One consistent example story runs through the Cart/Payments/Orders folders: buyer 'Order Test Buyer' adds 2x 'Order Test Sneaker' (₦15,000 each) to their cart from seller 'Order Test Store', pays via Paystack, and the seller marks the resulting order fulfilled. The Rewards folder follows a separate but equally real story: a ₦20,000 order earns 200,000 points (10 pts/₦1), which sit PENDING for 7 days, then become ACTIVE once the hold passes — at which point redeeming them is still blocked today because the monthly redemption cap is based on *last month's* real fulfilled GMV, which is ₦0 pre-revenue. All sample values below are taken from real responses during backend testing — shapes are accurate, specific IDs will differ per request.

request.description: Required `size`/`color` only if the product defines those options; must be one of the product's own values. Adding the same product+size+color again merges quantity into the existing line instead of duplicating it.

response.name: 201 Created
400 Bad Request — missing required size
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "Select a size for this product" }

response.name: 200 OK
200 OK

request.description: Public, no auth. Use this to get the Paystack publishable key instead of hardcoding it in the frontend.

`pointsToRedeem` is optional, defaults to 0 — omit the body entirely (or send `{}`) for a normal checkout with no points applied.

Prices and validates whatever is currently in the buyer's cart (same stock/active checks as cart add), then — if `pointsToRedeem > 0` — validates the redemption (see loyalty rules below) and subtracts the resulting ₦ discount from the amount actually charged to Paystack. Does NOT create any Order or deduct points yet, and does NOT touch stock/cart — that, and recording the points spend, only happens once payment is verified as successful (see Verify below).

Redemption rules, enforced in this order (see `GET /rewards` → `redemption` for the live numbers):
1. `pointsToRedeem` must be 0, or at least the account minimum (1,000 by default).
2. Can't exceed the buyer's available (ACTIVE) point balance.
3. The ₦ value of the points can't exceed a fixed % of this order's subtotal (10% by default) — sellers are never shorted their full order value.
4. The total ₦ value of points redeemed by *everyone* this calendar month can't exceed a small % of *last month's* total fulfilled-order GMV (1% by default). In a month with no prior fulfilled GMV, this is 0 — redemption is unavailable until there's a track record of real sales. This is deliberate, not a bug.

Use `accessCode` to open Paystack's Inline.js popup (recommended — card + bank transfer channels, card data never touches our backend), or redirect the browser to `authorizationUrl` for the hosted checkout page. Both show the same two channels since the backend restricts `channels: ["card", "bank_transfer"]`.

response.name: 201 Created — with points redeemed
response._comment: amount is what Paystack actually charges (order total minus pointsDiscount). Illustrative — see the note below on why redemption is 0-capped pre-revenue.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — below minimum redemption
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "You need at least 1000 points to redeem" }

response.name: 400 Bad Request — insufficient points balance
response._comment: Real response from testing: a brand-new buyer with no order history has 0 available points.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — exceeds 10% of this order
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "Points can cover at most 10% of this order (₦2000.00)" }

response.name: 400 Bad Request — monthly redemption cap reached
response.body: { "status": false, "message": "Points redemption has hit this month's limit — please try again next month or pay the full amount" }
response._comment: Real response from testing: with ₦0 fulfilled GMV last month, this cap is 0, so ANY redemption attempt is rejected right now — expected pre-revenue behavior, not a bug.

request.description:
Call this right after Paystack redirects back / the Inline popup resolves, passing the same `reference` from Initialize. This is what actually confirms payment with Paystack server-to-server AND creates the Order(s) — one per seller in the cart — decrements stock, clears the cart, and (if this checkout redeemed points) records the points spend against the buyer's balance.

Idempotent: calling it again for an already-paid reference just returns the same orders again, it will not double-charge, double-create, or double-deduct points.

item.name: Seller: get received order by id

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
status must be FULFILLED or CANCELLED. Only works while the order is still PENDING.

Marking FULFILLED also credits the buyer 10 points per ₦1 of the order's subtotal (see the Rewards folder) — those points sit PENDING for 7 days before they're spendable, then become ACTIVE automatically. There's no separate request for this; it's a side effect of this one.

Everything the Rewards screen needs in one call: tier, progress to the next tier, pending vs. spendable points, the live redemption settings (so the FE never hardcodes the rate/min/max), and a history feed.

Tier is based on fulfilled orders in the trailing 12 months, not lifetime spend — it can go back down if a buyer goes quiet for a year (same mechanism airlines use for status). `points.pending` are earned-but-not-yet-spendable (still inside the 7-day hold after the order was marked fulfilled); `points.available` is what can actually be redeemed right now. `history` entries are typed `EARN`/`REDEEM` with a `status` of `PENDING`/`ACTIVE` (an EARN row flips from PENDING to ACTIVE automatically once its hold passes — this response doesn't change shape, just that one field, between the two example states below).

response.name: 200 OK — brand new buyer, no history
response._comment: Real response from testing, for a freshly signed-up buyer with zero orders.

response.name: 200 OK — just earned points, still in the 7-day hold
response._comment: Real response from testing: a ₦20,000 order marked fulfilled earns 200,000 points (10/₦1) at 'Earn' rate, sitting PENDING until availableAt (fulfilled time + 7 days).

response.name: 200 OK — hold passed, points now spendable
response._comment: Real response from testing: same row, same id — only `status` flipped PENDING -> ACTIVE once the hourly sweep job passed its availableAt time, and the balance moved from pending to available accordingly.

response.name: 200 OK — after a redemption
